metadata.case_name: LEE CHING POR v. BAN WU

injuries.description: subtrochanteric fracture of the right femur
injuries.body_part: right femur / right thigh / right hip
source: deformed right thigh and the fractured femur
Mr. Lee had a fracture of right femur in the accident

manifestations.description: considerable pain in his leg, which had been crushed by the falling metal; pain was still severe and lasted about four days, necessitating pain killers
lost consciousness almost immediately after the accident, regaining it in the hospital a couple of hours later
residual pain and stiffness of the right hip
hip movement was restricted in flexion of 90° (left hip flexion : 120°)
a 22 cms scar in the lateral side of the upper part of the thigh; a bony prominence was felt in the fracture site; mild pain in the scar and the bony prominence
hip flexion and abduction power was weaker than the left hip
can walk on tip-toe and on heels with some difficulty
unable to do more than light work; cannot return to heavy labour on the construction site because of the weakness in his right thigh
no longer able to swim, nor to play ball games such as football or basketball

treatments_received: The latter was fixed with plates and screws on 7th April 1987, whereafter post-operative recovery was uneventful.
Normal walking was resumed six months after the accident
transferred to Pok Oi Hospital for physiotherapy after the operation
he underwent intensive physiotherapy for two years before he could walk independently.
the plates and screws were removed in April 1989 after sound union of the bone.

losses.description: residual stiffness and weakness of the right hip

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: no longer able to swim, nor to play ball games such as football or basketball
cannot return to heavy labour on the construction site; suitable for light jobs such as casual worker, messenger or lift operator
